item.title: Physics consistent conditional flow matching model as a plasma physics surrogate model
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 José Afonso, Pedro Viegas, Rodrigo Ventura and Vasco Guerra
Physics-informed surrogate modeling for steady-state systems often struggles with data scarcity and optimization instabilities from soft penalty losses. Unlike prevailing physics-informed generative methods that rely on explicit, differentiable PDE residuals during training, our framework targets systems where closed-form governing equations are unavailable or non-differentiable. We introduce a unified continuous-time conditional flow matching (CFM) framework for surrogate modeling and sparse data assimilation, evaluated on low-temperature plasma dynamics. By combining data-dependent interpolants with dynamic masking, our approach handles unconditioned prediction and missing-data imputation within a single architecture. We replace standard velocity matching with a direct state-prediction…

item.title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within o(N⁻¹/²) in the Replica Symmetric Phase
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham
arXiv:2610.32649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is o(N⁻¹/²) per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.
